note.coverage: Number theory, additive and extremal combinatorics, group theory, geometry, topology, analysis and optimization have individually located candidates as well as literature entry points.
note.gaps: The collection is uneven within mathematics. Representation theory beyond groups, arithmetic geometry beyond landmark conjectures, numerical analysis and specialized PDE programs need deeper coverage and full cards.
note.reason: The selection draws heavily on Kourovka, Green's collection and K3. These concentrations provide useful entry points, but numbered questions from a few collections are not a representative census of mathematical research.

note.coverage: The Kourovka selections cover algorithmic groups, finite and infinite groups, group rings and related structural questions. Exact finite-field and matroid tasks provide additional entry points.
note.gaps: Categories, homological algebra, noncommutative geometry and computational algebra beyond the selected sources remain thin. General group questions need modern follow-up checks.
note.reason: Kourovka problem numbers and the distinction between accepted resolutions and unconfirmed claims are preserved. The selection does not exhaust the notebook or the broader algebra literature.

note.coverage: Classical conjectures and individually numbered additive, multiplicative and prime-distribution questions are indexed alongside selected arithmetic geometry problems.
note.gaps: Automorphic forms, arithmetic statistics, effective Diophantine geometry and algorithmic number theory need further specialist sources and precise subproblems.
note.reason: A finite verification supports only the inspected range; altered quantifiers or extra hypotheses can change the problem.
note.remaining: The Littlewood and Lehmer problems and odd perfect numbers have explicit targets. Erdős–Straus retains conflicting proof claims, without a judgment of their correctness. New bounded tasks need a current status source and an independent verification plan.

note.coverage: Candidate records include convex and discrete geometry, knots, manifolds, surfaces, mapping classes and geometric algorithms. The K3 selections provide individually numbered topology questions.
note.gaps: Higher-dimensional, equivariant and stable homotopy theory remain underrepresented. Many K3 and computational geometry entries still need later-literature checks.
note.reason: Distinct notions of equivalence, smoothness and allowed geometric operations must be preserved in each statement.

note.coverage: The directory includes classical analytic conjectures, dynamical questions, spectral problems and systems governed by differential equations.
note.gaps: Harmonic analysis, operator algebras, nonlinear PDE and rigorous numerics need more full research cards and systematic status review.
note.reason: Convergence, regularity and boundary assumptions must be explicit; numerical evidence does not establish a general existence theorem.
note.status_limits: Caustic integrability has an explicit target. The Hilbert invariant-subspace problem retains conflicting proof claims, without a judgment of their correctness.

note.coverage: Finite constructions, control design and selected convex and nonconvex optimization questions connect symbolic and numerical methods.
note.gaps: Polynomial optimization hierarchies, real algebraic geometry and global-complexity bounds need dedicated problem collections.
note.reason: A local optimum, a numerical objective and a certified global bound are separate results.

note.coverage: The index spans Ramsey theory, set systems, graph constructions, additive combinatorics and finite geometric configurations. Individually numbered questions from Green's collection cover several methods and objectives.
note.gaps: Design theory, enumerative and algebraic combinatorics, extremal hypergraphs and probabilistic combinatorics remain unevenly covered.
note.reason: Related parameters share evidence, but distinct quantifiers and objectives should not be collapsed. A later result may resolve one variant while leaving a neighboring question open.

note.coverage: Complexity, computational geometry, algorithms, formal methods, rewriting and learning theory have individual candidates. Historical geometric and rewriting collections need checks for later resolutions; the absence of a solved marker is insufficient.
note.gaps: Cryptographic assumptions, distributed computation, fine-grained complexity and parameterized algorithms need broader specialist review.
note.reason: Input encoding, arithmetic model, randomness, approximation and worst-case versus amortized guarantees are part of the statement.

note.gaps: Finite model theory, constructive mathematics and independence programs need more full cards. Historical lists require careful status checks.
note.reason: Independence is relative to specified axioms; a proof in a stronger theory does not automatically answer a question about a weaker one.

note.gaps: Stochastic analysis, interacting particle systems, random matrices and quantitative limit theory need more current specialist sources.
note.reason: Finite simulation, convergence in distribution, almost-sure behavior and uniform bounds are different targets.

note.gaps: Semiparametric efficiency, adaptive inference, dependence, robust uncertainty quantification and experimental design remain unevenly covered. Some proceedings abstracts identify a target whose full assumptions still need to be recovered.
note.reason: Population guarantees and finite-data benchmarks require separate assumptions and validation.

area: Quantum field theory and mathematical physics

note.coverage: Yang–Mills and mass-gap questions appear alongside particle-physics targets concerning the electroweak hierarchy, neutrinos and strong CP.
note.scope: Axiomatic construction, mass gaps and effective-field-theory assumptions.
note.remaining: Yang–Mills still needs an actionable decomposition. Constructive field theory, scattering amplitudes and renormalization need broader specialist sources. A short statement does not make a Millennium problem tractable.

area: Statistical mechanics and condensed matter theory

note.coverage: Ising and Ornstein–Uhlenbeck calibration cards accompany candidates on many-body localization, thermalization, subdiffusion and avalanches.
note.scope: Exactly specified lattice and stochastic models with separate physical interpretation.
note.remaining: Interacting systems, disorder, glasses, critical phenomena and nonequilibrium theory need deeper coverage. Simple solvable models do not represent their resource requirements.
note.status_limits: The 2026 fixed-energy light-cone theorem does not establish infinite-temperature or finite-energy-density localization throughout a spin chain's spectrum.

area: Classical mechanics, fluids and plasma theory

note.coverage: Celestial-mechanics calibration tasks and dynamo candidates provide examples of formal dynamics and fluid models.
note.scope: Rotating-frame dynamics, low-Prandtl small-scale dynamos and magnetorotational instability under specified assumptions.
note.remaining: Continuum mechanics, kinetic theory, turbulence and plasma models need broader coverage and detailed cards. Model closure and boundary assumptions require separate empirical evidence.
note.status_limits: Low-Prandtl dynamo existence has been demonstrated in particular geometries. The retained questions concern saturation, a specified transition limit and controlled extrapolation; geometry-specific results cannot be transferred without argument.

note.coverage: Candidates cover cosmic censorship, black-hole geometry, cosmological singularities, approximation limits and cosmological mechanisms.
note.scope: Spacetime geometry, gravitational dynamics, cosmological models and vacuum-energy assumptions.
note.remaining: Many broad targets need specialist status reviews and precise subproblems. Formal consistency and observational adequacy require separate evidence.
note.status_limits: General subextremal Kerr nonlinear stability is excluded as an open candidate because Peter Hintz's August 2026 preprint claims a solution under specified initial-data hypotheses. The proof claim requires specialist review and does not establish Penrose's large-data final-state conjecture.

note.coverage: Lagrange-point and Jacobi calibration tasks accompany central-configuration, choreography, variational and scattering questions.

note.remaining: Many questions in the historical celestial-mechanics collection need later-literature checks. Nonlinear stability, resonances, collisions, stellar and galactic dynamics, radiative processes and cosmological perturbations need more detailed cards. No observational dataset has received a task-specific audit.
note.status_limits: The all-positive-mass planar five-body finiteness claim is a status-change lead, not an independently audited theorem. The six-body question remains a separate target.

area: Chemical reaction networks and systems biology

note.coverage: Deterministic and stochastic networks are represented by structural, long-term-behavior and biological-regulation questions, together with constrained generation, graph realizability and infinite-network targets.
note.gaps: Spatial reaction systems, inference of mechanisms and experimentally constrained biochemical control require more detailed treatment.

note.scope: Pattern formation, neural dynamics, synthetic multicellularity, regulatory mechanisms and coupling between biological scales.
note.remaining: Mechanistic questions need explicit models, measurable outputs and suitable data before bounded tasks can be specified. Model reduction can be formal; identifying biological mechanisms may require new experiments. Large simulations need separate resource assessment.

note.remaining: Repeated, Bayesian, extensive-form and other stochastic games need broader coverage. An existence theorem alone supplies no empirical prediction.

note.scope: Preferences, aggregation, allocation, matching, incentives, equilibrium and dynamic macro models.

area: Fair allocation: distinctions between open and resolved cases

note.scope: Complete four-agent goods EFX0 through nine goods and EFX for cancelable multigraph goods have positive results. These bounded or structured results are not listed as unsolved tasks. Additive-chore counterexamples exist for every n≥4, while the narrower common bi-valued question remains open.

Zhang reports seven- and eight-chore existence and gives a dated open-status statement for nine. A subsequent anonymous release claims nine-chore existence but explicitly lacks established independent verification or specialist review. Nine chores is therefore not recommended as a confirmed open target; the unrestricted cardinality question is recorded separately.
The negative binary XOS and supermodular results do not settle the remaining submodular question. A theorem for goods with binary marginal gains is not automatically a theorem for chore costs.

note.gaps: Network formation, temporal networks, causal interventions and epidemic control need broader sources and model-specific cards.

The general two-state avoiding conjecture is deferred because the older conjecture and newer summary require reconciliation. The indexed formulation excludes unavoidable subsets.

note: All seven Millennium and 23 Hilbert entries have historical status records. Solved entries do not count as open candidates. Broad programs and formulation-sensitive cases still need specialist primary-source histories and individually scoped research questions.

Graph, tournament and multiplication-table group isomorphism are related algorithmic targets, with the latter two restricted subproblems of the first. Classical and infinitary Vaught conjectures are distinct strengths. Martin's two parts have different conclusions. These links should be retained when selecting a project to avoid counting one result twice.

The Unique Games conjecture is deferred because of the September 2026 full-resolution claim at https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/The-Unique-Games-Theorem-September-23-2026/build/sections/00-introduction.tex. Matrix multiplication exponent 2 is deferred because of https://chinarxiv.org/items/chinaxiv-202609.00167. These claims require independent specialist review.

The Courtade–Kumar most-informative-Boolean-function conjecture is not listed as an open target because https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24931 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.24184 announce complete proofs. Their validity and publication status require specialist review.

The arXiv record 2603.23561 is withdrawn and reports an incorrect Lemma 2 proof; it does not establish a solution to sample compression. The ECCC 2026/043 revision at https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2026/043/revision/1/download/ is a retraction note identifying a conditioning gap, so its claimed multilinear-branching-program barrier is not used.

Every main domain has multiple primary records, but many subfields still have only entry sources or provisional outlines. Set-theoretic independence, numerical analysis, cryptography, solid-Earth theory and cognitive science beyond neural modeling remain priorities for broader source review.

Mathematical model questions, mechanism identification and observational tensions have different success criteria. Conditional derivations, model comparison and existing-data analysis can support bounded theoretical work. Identifying the actual physical or biological mechanism may require new observations or complex experiments. Each proposed model or restricted subproblem needs its own novelty and evidence review; a broad unresolved question does not establish either.

note.evidence: A located source statement, a dated resolution search and a scientific review establish different things. Historical open labels and unreviewed proof claims are recorded with their limits. None establishes that no later resolution exists. Source-defined variants retain their relationship to the broader question.
note.assessment: Difficulty and AI-role profiles are dated, untested forecasts. No named model has been evaluated. Profiles with insufficient evidence retain an unknown rating; source inspection and a profile do not replace a full methods assessment or a signed scientific review.
note.resources: Small witnesses can be easy to check while exhaustive searches remain expensive. Proposed resource ceilings are stop rules, not measured costs or predictions of success. No success rate, runtime or expenditure has been measured.
note.next_steps: Before an attempt, check the exact definitions, remaining parameter regimes, current status, significance and independent verification plan. Curator-proposed restrictions on agents, items, graphs or computation are possible first steps whose separate novelty and feasibility remain unverified.
